question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $(2x-\frac{1}{2})\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $P$ has velocity $1\,m/s$ when its displacement is $1\,m,$ find the values of $x$ for which $P$ is instantaneously at rest.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14273713/assets/6046ef89f9abcc78be695d69df64471fb9c68645473c946e7f3212be27e2c6fb.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(2x-\frac{1}{2})\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=2x-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=2x-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (2x-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}x+C.
$$

Now, since $v=1\,m/s$ when $x=1\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}x+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(1)^{2} & =(1)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}(1)+C \\ C & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\ C & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}x.
$$

Finally, the particle is instantaneously at rest when $v(x)=0\,m/s.$ We find the displacement of the particle when instantaneously at rest by substituting $v=0$ in the equation above and solving for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}x \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & ={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}x \\ {x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}x & =0 \\ x(x-\frac{1}{2}) & =0 \\ x & =0\,m,\,\frac{1}{2}\,m.\end{aligned}
$$
